plan.english: "Shepherd, are your sheep good?" "They are good and strong, stranger. This ram is strong. The wool is thick. Sit down and look at them." "I am looking." "I seek wool." "What do you give?" "I have no gold. I give two he-goats." "Two he-goats?" "Two he-goats and two lambs!" "Three lambs." "Four lambs!" "I give three." "Let it be so, and take the wool." "May the gods protect you." Then he bound the wool with a cord and carried the load. The dog followed him. He was sweating. He sat down under the hazel by the marsh. A crane was standing there. Then he rose, went on, and made a hymn of praise.

"Brother, where are the cattle?" "I drove them to the field." "Did you see the wolf?" "I did not see the wolf; I heard the dog." "Then stand up, go to the field, and lead them home." "I will go. Sit, and drink water." Night came. Then he went to the field, and he cried out. The dog heard and ran, and saw them at the water. He led them home. "May the gods protect you." They had become tired and thirsty. They drank and became sated. His heart rejoiced, and he lay down. At dawn he woke up and caught sight of them. They stood at the door, and he cried out with joy.

"Husband, there is no wool in the home. It has grown cold. What shall I do?" "Go to the shepherd, and buy wool. What price does he say?" "He says two sheep." "Do not give them to him. The price is great. I will give him a lamb and a he-goat. The he-goat is strong. I will clothe you with wool." "May the gods protect you." Then he went to him. That one heard his words. The wife put the wool in order and clothed the sons. They became warm and did not tremble. The sons sat around the fire, and the fire burned up. The wife said: "The wool is the gift of the gods."

"Shepherd, I am king. Hear me, and give me wool and a ram." "King, I hear you. I give you wool and a ram. Lambs I do not give; I protect them with my dog." "Who guards you?" "The dog guards me." "Take gold." "Gold I do not eat. Give me the field." "The field is broad and good. I will give it to you. Let us set a pledge. Dyeus is witness. If one deceives the other, may Perkunos kill him." "Carry the wool and the ram to the village." "I will carry them." Then the king's troops arrived and carried the ram away. He stood at the door and looked at the field. The king spoke to the queen: "He is a knower." The queen said: "May the goddess protect him."

"Son, lead the ram to the village." "Mother, what shall I seek?" "Seek gold. When you have seen the gold, give the ram. Do not listen to the stranger's words." "I will go to the village." Then he went to the village and saw a stranger. That one spoke: "What do you lead?" "I lead a ram." "I give you gold." He saw the gold. He gave the ram to him and took the gold. Then he came home. "Mother, I gave the ram." "You are a man." The mother hid the gold. He sat down at the table, and he ate and drank. He said: "That one's eyes were burning." The mother listened. "Lie down. Sleep will come."

"Sit down. The fire burns, and the grain is cooking. Eat, and drink. Who are you? What is your name?" "My name is famous. I am a shepherd's son. I came to your village. I was thirsty, and I became tired." "Fill yourself." "I am satisfied. Father Sky, giver of good things, may you protect this man." "Come again." That one lay by the fire, and sleep seized him. The other was awake and kept looking at the door. A hedgehog lay under the hazel.

"Father, do you seek gold?" "Cattle I seek. Gold is not eaten. You do not milk gold. You milk cattle; they nourish the sons." "But gold is red, and the king buys them with gold." "If they die, what will you eat?" "Your word is good. I will not give them to the king." "May your name be famous." Now he remembers his father's word, and his work succeeded. Then the two sat down at the table and ate rye and garlic. The father's heart rejoiced.

"Brother, yesterday the wolf seized a lamb." "Which did he seize?" "The red lamb." "The wolf is big and swift." "Let us guard the sheep. Sit by the fire. If the wolf comes, what shall we do?" "We shall cry out, and the dog will tear the wolf." It grew dark, and the sun sank. The dog heard and cried out. The wolf was creeping. Then the two brothers stood up and threw spears. The wolf fled, and the sheep lived. At dawn the two saw blood. A fang lay on the earth. The dog was licking the blood. Then the two smeared themselves with fat and lay down.

"Brother, I seek a wife." "Whom do you seek out?" "I seek your sister." "My sister is dear. What bride price do you give?" "I give ten cattle and gold." "The bride price is much. Give also two swift horses." "Let us set a pledge." "I give you my sister." "Rejoice." "Mother, I go to his home." "Go. May Mother Earth guard you." The sister wore adorned clothing. The mother looked at her and cried out. The two horses pulled the wagon, and the sister sat in it.

"Man, where is my ram?" "I do not know." "You stole it!" "I did not steal. Who saw me?" "My two eyes saw you." "You lie to me. I bought the ram from the shepherd with gold." "Which shepherd? Say his name." "Let us go to the shepherd; he will speak." Then they arrived. "What do you seek?" "This man gave me gold, and I gave him a ram." "You did not steal. I have come to know it." The two sat down and drank. His heart trembled. The sun sank, and night came. The two went home and lay down.

It dawned. "Now I go." "Where do you go?" "I go to that village yonder." The sun shone. "Eat, and drink. Put on your shoes. This is my gift: take the wool." "I take your gift. May the gods give you a long life." "Carry water for the road. May the gods make your road straight, and come again." "Live, dear friend." He was walking, and the heat was growing. He arrived at the sea. In the evening he arrived and sat near a door. A woman was carrying water.

"Is this horse swift?" "He is swift and big. His neck is broad." "Is he a god?" "He is no god; his father drew the king's wagon." "What do you seek for him?" "I seek ten cattle." "Five cattle." "Seven." "Let it be so. Take the horse and yoke him. May he carry you." Then the horse ran. The men looked at him, and his fame grew. The hearts of the men were astonished. He drove him around.

"Who are you?" "I am a shepherd's son. I live in the village." "Where did you arrive?" "I arrived at the water." "What is your father's name?" "His name is famous." "Your father is a giver. I heard it. He gave my father a horse." "Have you a brother?" "A brother and a sister are mine." "You are my guest. Enter my home. May the gods guard this village." Then the two entered the home. The wife seated him and nourished him. The wife brought water in the washbasin.

"Yesterday I bought wool. The price was great." "What did you give?" "I gave a ram." "Last year the price was not great. The wool is good. Is it light?" "It is thick." "Show us the wool." "Will you buy again?" "I will not buy again, if he seeks much." "Let us go to the shepherd." "May his heart be good." Then the two went to him. He showed the wool. The wool was light, and the price was not great. They rejoiced.

Dawn shone. The women came to the village carrying wool, and the herdsmen were driving the sheep. The fire burned and the grain was cooking. Great was the voice of the men. "Come! See the wool! The wool is thick and the price is not great. Buy the ram!" A stranger sat down and kept looking at the horses. The smith was working, and the water was boiling. A snake crept toward the nest. The sun stood high.

"Women! Come, and look at the thick wool of this ram. Who will buy it?" A woman said: "What do you say the price is?" "Two lambs." "Your wool is thick, but the price is great. I will give you a lamb and a he-goat." "Give them to me, and take the wool." "May you have strong sons." The seller rejoiced and sat down on the seat. The women went home.

The king's man stood up and cried: "Hear! The king has proclaimed the price. The price of a head of cattle is ten sheep. The price of a ram is two sheep. Whoever deceives a man in trade, let him give ten sheep." The men heard. "The king's word is good," they said. The smith built a door and set it upright.

A man carrying gold came to the village. He was seeking swift horses. Then he saw two swift horses. "Smith, what do you say the price is for these horses?" "A hundred sheep." "I have no hundred sheep. I have gold." "Gold is good. Give gold and take the horses." Then he yoked them, and went. The smith was astonished, and he kept looking at the gold.

A stranger stole a ram. The dog saw him and cried out. The shepherd heard and ran. The stranger fled, but the shepherd seized him. "Where is the ram?" "I do not know." "You lie. My dog saw you." "Take the ram, and let me go." "Go, and do not come again." He was leaving the village, and the dog was following him.

It rained. The men fled to the shelter, and the wives covered the wool. "Come into the shelter! Great is the water of the sky!" They sat down in the shelter. "Dry the wool!" a woman said. The sheep were trembling. Then the sun shone, and the men stood up and bought again. The sun was heating the earth, and the men were going home.

The sun sank. It grew dark. The men went home. The shepherd sat by the fire and looked at the gold. He said: "The sheep went away; the gold came. The sale was good." He rejoiced, and the dog lay down. "Father Sky, guard the sheep!"

title: The Man Who Gave Away His Cattle

plan.english: A man gave all his cattle to the king and took gold. Then his sons were thirsty. Gold is not eaten. He sought them. No one gave them to him. Gold is not cattle, and gold does not live. His heart grew slack, and he cried out.

"I seek grain." "What do you carry?" "I carry a he-goat. It is strong." "I will acquire the he-goat with grain. Take much grain." "Let it be so." Then he led it away, and the other drove the grain home. The he-goat was devouring the grain.

"Where does he dwell who leads swift horses?" "He dwells yonder. Go to the water; there you will see the cow-stall. The horses are in the stall." "Your word is a gift to me." "May you see the horses." He went to the water. Now he has reached the stall.

"Hear my words! My name is famous. My father had good fame. I have swift horses. Who will buy?" "Famous man, what price do you say?" "My horses are swift; the price is ten cattle." "Seven cattle." "Take them. May your fame be imperishable." Thus he became rich.

"I do not deceive you. My sheep are strong. If I deceive you, may Perkunos kill me." "I trust you. Dyeus is listening. I will buy the ram. Let us set a pledge." "Take the ram." The sale was carried out successfully.

Two men came to the king. The first spoke: "I gave the horse. He gave me no gold." The other spoke: "I gave gold. Where is the horse? I did not see the horse." The king said: "Let us go to the cow-stall. If the horse is in the stall, let the other take it. If not, let the first give gold." They arrived. The horse lay in the stall, and the other took it.

"What is the price of the ram?" "Ten sheep." "The price is great. Four sheep." "The ram is strong. Eight." "Five." "Seven." "Six." "Let it be so. Take the ram, and lead it away." "May Dyeus watch us." Then he tied the ram with a cord.

"I seek wool. I have cattle." "What do you give?" "Three cattle." "The wool of a hundred sheep is much." "Five, and take the wool." "Let it be five. May your sheep be many." The cattle were going to the field.

"I give you the wagon. Give me the two horses." "Who will yoke them?" "I shall yoke them." "The wagon is strong." "The horses are swift." "I do not give the yoke." "Take also the yoke. Let us set a pledge." "Drive, and live." He drove them on.

"I give you my field. Give me a hundred sheep." "Last year much grain was growing. It is broad and good." "A hundred sheep are many. I will give you ten cattle and wool." "I gave you the field." "Mother Earth, guard this field!" Then he ploughed it.

"You deceived me!" "What have I done?" "This ram lay down and did not stand up." "The ram was strong. You saw it. I do not deceive you." "Take the ram, and give me the gold back." "I will give the gold. Go."

"Guard my sheep." "What wage do you say?" "Two lambs and wool." "That is much. I give you a lamb and wool, and you milk the sheep." "The wolves are many. I will guard them. May the wolf not come." "We have set a pledge." The dog was awake, and the wolf vanished.
"Father Sky, hear! Mother Earth, hear! I gave the ram. He gave gold. Whoever deceives the other, let him not live. We have set the pledge. The gods are witnesses. May the pledge stand."

title: The Law of Buying and Selling

plan.english: If a man steals cattle, let him give ten cattle. If a man buys a ram, let him give gold. If he does not give it, let the shepherd take the ram back. If a man deceives a stranger in trade, let him give the stranger ten sheep. If a man breaks the pledge, let him give ten sheep and gold.

title: The Man Who Traded in a Circle

plan.english: A man obtained grain with a he-goat. Then he obtained wool with the grain, and then a lamb with the wool, and then the he-goat again with the lamb. "What did you gain by trade?" "I gained fame. The he-goat is mine again."

title: I Do Not Sell, I Give

plan.english: "I seek a lamb. What price do you say?" "I ask no price from a guest. Take it; this is a gift." "I take it. I will give you wool." "A gift is not bought." "Then may you have good fame."

"I have seen my ram." "I bought the ram from a stranger with gold." "That one stole it." "I did not know." "Give me the ram, and I give you gold." "Is it much gold?" "It is not much." "May the gods seize him. Rejoice." The ram has come home.

"Your price is great." "My cattle are strong." "I will not buy them." "Then I will not give them to you." "I will go to the other." "Night is coming. Sit by the fire and eat. At dawn we will speak again." "Your fire is good. Let it be so." They ate and sipped.

The king said: "I shall give you swift horses. What will you give me?" The other king said: "I shall give you gold and a hundred sheep. The trade is great. Let us set a pledge. May we have good fame." The queen rejoiced.
